title: Separate organizations, same people at the top
question: Which City-funded organizations that do not declare each other as related list two or more of the same officers or directors?
finding: 11 pairs of City-funded organizations that do not report each other as related share two or more listed people in the same year; 7 pairs are paid by the same department, 1 pass grants between them and 0 file from the same address.
how: Every officer, director and key employee on each organization’s Form 990 Part VII is compared across organizations for the same tax year. Organizations that name each other on Schedule R, or share the first two words of their name, are treated as one family and skipped. Two shared names are required (three if the names are common), which makes coincidence unlikely.
limits: Shared directors are common between a parent charity and the housing or service corporations it sponsors, which do not always appear on Schedule R. The concern is narrower: two organizations presented to the City as independent bidders or as an arm’s-length grantor and grantee while the same people control both.
